[ECCR (KDD 2024)](https://assets.amazon.science/6a/b5/41364589408ead2fc48043b0ea5c/eccr-explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models.pdf) distinguishes broad complementarity from item-level relevance and compatibility: a screen protector can complement a phone yet target the wrong device. Implication for diagnostics: classify substitute/complement relationships separately from compatibility; similarity or co-occurrence alone cannot establish useful complements or redundant purchases. Interaction histories establish observed interactions, not current ownership, equipment availability, replacement intent, or whether an earlier item remains usable.

[Sufficient Context (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06037) separates insufficient evidence from failure to use available evidence; [Knowing What’s Missing (2025, revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06476) identifies missing facts and then verifies their absence against source text. Adapt these principles without importing pretrained weights: extract literal title/description spans for model identifiers, connectors, dimensions, supported devices, exclusions, and accessory requirements. Record relation, judgment, supporting spans, and missing fields. Use supported-compatible, explicitly-incompatible, and unknown outcomes; an omitted specification is unknown. Flag potential redundancy only when text establishes matching identity/function, leaving purchase necessity unresolved.

Proposed evaluation: manually review a small sample stratified across four categories and all judgment types, including abstentions; double-annotate a subset and adjudicate disagreements. Measure precision separately for incompatibility, complement, and redundancy flags; also report coverage, abstention rate, evidence-span correctness, and sample counts with confidence intervals. Include missing-specification and conflicting-specification cases. These are proposed diagnostics, not established benchmark results; retain macro validation HR@10 for model selection.
